transcript: The night before your birthday, sit alone for five minutes. No phone, no music, no one else in the room. Light a candle. This candle represents the year that's ending. While it burns, say out loud, everything you're ready to let go of. You don't need to explain it, just name it. The anger, the doubt, the person who hurt you, the mistake you keep replaying in your head. Say it and let the flame hold it. Then blow out the candle, not to make a wish, to mark the ending, immediately light a new candle. This one represents the year that's beginning. While it burns, say what you want to invite into your life. Peace, clarity, courage, health, abundance. Say each word slowly and feel it. Leave the second candle burning until it goes out on its own, or until you fall asleep. When you wake up on your birthday, you're going to feel lighter. Not because of magic, because you chose to let go of something before picking up something new. Most people enter a new year, carrying everything from the previous one. The same fears, the same wounds, the same people, the same thoughts. And they wonder why the new year looks so much like the old one, because they never closed what was left open. This ritual gives you a moment to do it. Five minutes of silence, where you tell your life, this stays here, this comes with me.
